Definition: from G1519 and πηδάω (to leap); to rush in:--run (spring) in.
BiblicalUsage: This word means to leap or rush in, and it occurs once, in the Philippian jail. The keeper calls for a light, springs in trembling, and falls down before Paul and Silas, asking what he must do to be saved. One rush into a prison cell becomes the beginning of a household's salvation.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God can turn a jailer's terror into faith in a single night, because the earthquake shook the prison and the gospel shook the man.
RelatedEvents: Paul and Silas in the Philippian Prison
